> (CDH3beta). After running the sample, the /tmp/top seems to have just
> a sequence file containing the lines of the text file with line
> numbers (not counts). I may have missed something.
>

The code is wrong:

replace  y <- strsplit(unlist(map.values)," ") with  y <- unlist(strsplit(unlist(map.values)," "))

I can mail a slide later tonight.

The 'result is 256' is quite useless. I'll remove it one day.

Cheers

Saptarshi

messages.subject: Tools for debugging/profiling Map reduce job
messages.subject_clean: Tools for debugging/profiling Map reduce job
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
Is there any tools available for debugging map reduce jobs.

I know some of the ways of debugging like:

1. As suggested by you like using rhex interatively

2. using tryCatch block

For profiling we need to use system.time to get the time consumed by
different segments of code, and outputting via rhcollect and rhcounter

Regards,
Som

Hello,

Unfortunately, I havent had the time to think about a framework for debugging.
HAdoop has something related to debug scripts that can be executed on
the offending 'split'.
I could (in future) look towards using that. It might be of help.
but yes, currently, debugging can be, to say the least, adventurous.

My priority now is to add a custom multiple file output format - i.e.
based on the key value write to different
output directories.

Regards
J

reported that they have managed to get Hadoop running successfully on
Windows without the help of Cygwin.

Assuming that it is possible to get Hadoop running natively on
Windows. Is it possible to build and configure RHIPE on Windows,
without the help of Cygwin? Is it possible to get RHIPE working with
the help of Cygwin?

Cheers
Adrian,

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] RHIPE on Windows
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adrian,

The way it is written (now), RHIPE communicates over standard error
and output. I have no experience
coding on Windows, and dont know if these work.
Also, there is some UNIX specific stuff in the R portion (though that
can be made cross platform).

In short,  i wouldn't wait for a Windows version. I personally do not
use Windows.

Regards

Saptarshi

messages.body_plain:
Hmm distilling it down to a minimum test case revealed that it
worked.  I changed it to pass environments instead of list and
attached that environment in the setup prior to map/reduce.  Seems to
work.  Gives an output of 5.0 for each time the mapper was invoked.

rhmrWithEnvSetup = function(env.setup, ...){

	mc = match.call()
	mc = as.list(mc)
	if(!is.null(mc$setup)){

		cat("Error: env setup currently incompatable with setup argument.

\n")
	}

	mc[[1]] = NULL 	    # removes call from list

	mc$env.setup = NULL #removes from list
	env.setup = rawToChar(serialize(env.setup,NULL,ascii=TRUE))
	print(env.setup)
	if(!is.null(mc$mapred)){
		mc$mapred$env.setup = env.setup
	}else{
		mc$mapred = list()
		mc$mapred$env.setup = env.setup
	}
	setup = expression({
    	env.setup =  unserialize( charToRaw( Sys.getenv("env.setup") ))
    	attach(env.setup)
    	print(ls())

	})
	mc$setup = setup
	return(do.call("rhmr", mc))

}

mapper = expression({
	rhcollect(1,test.function())
})

env.setup = new.env()
env.setup$test.function = function(){
	return(5)
}
DIR = getwd()
args = list()
args$map = mapper
args$env.setup = env.setup
args$ifolder = paste(DIR,"input",sep="/")
args$ofolder = paste(DIR,"output", sep="/")
args$inout = c("text","text")
args$mapred = list(mapred.job.tracker='local')
mr = do.call("rhmrWithEnvSetup", args)
rhex(mr)
